Subject: Dedicated capacity: scheduled maintenance impact and SLA carve-out request

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking our call earlier. We are finalizing our Dedicated capacity purchase (DEAL-20478) but the procurement team flagged a recurring scheduled maintenance window that your ops team runs on the west coast cluster (SFO region). Our production traffic has strict 6am-10am PST peak windows; the maintenance currently overlaps that and in the past caused 200-400ms latency spikes and short-lived queueing.

Before we sign, we need an explicit carve-out clause or operational runbook that ensures:
- No maintenance within our declared peak window without a 72-hour notice and opt-in
- A fallback policy (automatic routing to a compatible hosted variant) when preemptive maintenance is required
- A credit calculation method if sustained latency > 200ms for >5m during peak hours

Attached is our maintenance calendar and the list of endpoints we consider latency-sensitive. Can you confirm whether Redwood can scope a contractual exception or provide an ops-runbook we can review?

Appreciate a timeline — procurement would like this wrapped this week.

Best,
Laura
Laura Chen
VP of Infrastructure, Cascade AI

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear summary and the calendar. Looping in Karthik (pricing & SLA), Jonas (infra/ops), and Marissa (customer success / commercial).

Quick answers up-front:
- We can propose a contractual amendment that defines a maintenance carve-out for declared peak windows and sets notification timelines.
- We have an automated fallback mechanism that can route traffic to a hosted-compatible model; the tradeoff is a predictable increase in per-token cost and a slightly higher P99. We can include the fallback as an explicit mitigation path.
- For crediting, we typically tie credits to sustained SLO breaches measured at the per-route P95/P99 level; we can draft an arithmetic credit schedule aligned with your requirement (e.g., if P99 > 200ms for >5 minutes then X% credit).

Jonas — can you confirm technical feasibility for excluding scheduled maintenance from your SFO pool during the 6am-10am PST windows and outline the runbook (notification hooks, automated failover, and canary window)?

Karthik / Marissa — I’ll draft a proposed amendment and commercial language once we have the ops details. Laura — we can aim to get a draft over today for procurement review and a DocuSign link if that works.

Thanks,
Naomi

Naomi / Laura — quick technical note from infra ops:

1) Maintenance carve-out feasibility
We can schedule node-level maintenance to avoid a tenant's declared peak windows. For Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) we maintain maintenance cohorts; excluding Cascade AI's pool from the default maintenance cohort is operationally trivial if agreed contractually and scheduled in advance. This requires:
- A maintenance exclusion flag for the tenant pool (we'll need signed authorization)
- A minimum 72-hour lock on changes to the exclusion list to avoid churn during mass updates

2) Automated fallback
We support an automated fallback path that will:
- Detect maintenance-triggered capacity pressure (based on queue depth + KV cache hot failures)
- Signal the routing layer to use the nominated hosted model variant (same family, lower perf profile)
- Emit tracing tags and a rollback token so we can invoice credits accurately
Tradeoffs: small P99 increase and transient token-cost spike. We can cap the fallback duration to avoid unbounded costs.

3) Measurement and credits
Our monitoring captures per-route latency at 10s resolution and keeps 90-day retention. For credits, we propose:
- If P99 > 200ms for >= 5 continuous minutes during your declared peak window, then 5% monthly service credit per incident, capped at 20% per billing period.
- An incident must be validated by both parties (monitoring links + sampling traces).

4) Runbook sketch (high level)
- T-72h: Ops sends maintenance notice to customer and creates a maintenance ticket in the shared folder.
- T-24h: Automated canary run to ensure failover path is healthy (dry-run with synthetic traffic).
- Maintenance window: If emergency maintenance required within peak, we execute fallback and notify via webhook and email.
- Post-maintenance: 1-hour validation, provide traces and latency summary.

I attached a short ops-runbook (see Drive link Naomi included) and will follow up with specific API hooks we need for your side to accept routing signals.

-- Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Thanks Jonas — that all looks reasonable. Commercial note from my side:

We can offer the maintenance carve-out and the fallback guarantee as part of the Dedicated contract as an SLA amendment. Key commercial terms I propose:
- Maintenance carve-out: excluded windows are customer-declared (max 2 recurring weekly windows), 72-hour notice for changes. No extra recurring fee for the carve-out itself.
- Fallback execution: free for the first 3 emergency events per 12-month period, thereafter a small per-event failover fee (to account for hosting delta) or a blended rate applied to tokens routed to hosted variants.
- Credit schedule: use Jonas' proposed crediting math. We will require joint incident validation and an SLA claim window of 14 days after the event.

I will prepare the amendment text and attach a commercial addendum: proposed language, examples of credit calculation, and the DocuSign envelope for signature. Naomi — feel free to add any negotiation levers before I send.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Product Commercialization, Redwood Inference

- Credit schedule: P99 > 200ms for >=5 continuous minutes during peak => 5% credit per incident, capped 20% for the billing period. Joint validation required within 14 days.
